## What changed

This Next.js 16 canary uses the new `prefetch()` API from `next/cache` (introduced in v16.4.0, replacing `unstable_prefetch`), which works together with Partial Prefetching. The three-stage model is: App Shell (every `<Link>` prefetches by default) → per-link prefetch (`<Link prefetch={true}>`) → navigation.

**`next.config.ts`** — added `partialPrefetching: true`. This is required for `prefetch()` to have any effect; without it a route has no App Shell. It also changes the default `<Link>` prefetch to fetch only the App Shell rather than the full page.

**`app/product/page.tsx`** — moved the related-products list into a `<RelatedProducts>` async component wrapped in `<Suspense>`, and added `await prefetch()` before `getRelatedProducts()`. Per the docs, `prefetch()` keeps everything below it out of the App Shell, so the cached related-products data is *not* generated on a plain/default product-page prefetch — only the Suspense fallback is. (Note: `prefetch()` must sit outside the `use cache` scope, which it does here — it's awaited in the component, and the `'use cache'` directive stays on `getRelatedProducts`.)

**`app/page.tsx`** — set `prefetch={true}` on the featured-product `<Link>`. This opts into a per-link prefetch that resolves the URL-specific content deferred by `prefetch()`, so the related products are fetched and ready immediately when the user navigates from that link.

## How it satisfies the request

- **Related products out of the default prefetch:** A plain `<Link href="/product">` (or any other link into the route) prefetches only the App Shell — the static shell plus the Suspense fallback. `getRelatedProducts()` is not called, so no related-products work happens.
- **Ready immediately from the featured-product link:** `<Link prefetch={true}>` triggers a per-link prefetch that runs the deferred subtree, resolving the cached related-products data ahead of the click. On navigation the content is already there.

One thing to note: I chose `prefetch()` rather than `navigation()` deliberately — `navigation()` would also exclude the content from per-link prefetches, which would defeat the "ready immediately from the featured link" requirement. `prefetch()` is the one that resolves on a per-link prefetch.

14	`partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more.
15	
16	## Usage
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} switcher

20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {

27	```

31	  cacheComponents: true,
32	  partialPrefetching: true,
33	}
34	```

36	`partialPrefetching` requires [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). Without it, `next dev` and `next build` throw at config validation.
37	
38	## Reference
39	
40	| Value   | Description                                 |
41	| ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
42	| `true`  | Enables Partial Prefetching across the app. |
43	| `false` | Default. No change to prefetch behavior.    |
44	
45	## How prefetches resolve
46	
47	Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced ~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport.
48	
49	With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. 50	
51	The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it.
52	
53	> **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client.
54	
55	A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
56	
57	> **Good to know**: If you use `<Link prefetch={true}>` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail.
58	
59	## Per-segment overrides
60	
61	A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route.
62	
63	## Version History
64	
65	| Version | Change                                                                     |
66	| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
67	| 16.3.0  | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. |
